newsitem.title: UK: Unilever takes 32 million pound charge in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Unilever takes 32 million pound charge in Q3.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc announced a five percent rise in profits on Friday to 826 million pounds ($1.36 billion) over the latest three months and took exceptional charges of 32 million pounds, mostly to cover re-shaping its industrial cleaning business Diversey.

Over the nine month period, pretax profits rose two percent to 1.951 billion on sales of 25.24 billion, a rise of eight percent on the previous nine month period. The company announced a dividend for the half year of 10.29p per five pence ordinary share of Unilever Plc, an increase of 46 percent from last year.

Diversey, acquired in January from Canadian brewer Molson for 360 million stg, was merged with Lever Industrial in October to form a combined business with annual turnover of 1.15 billion and a workforce of 13,000 in 60 countries.

"Although poor weather had a negative effect on icecream sales, other parts of the business in Europe did well," said Unilever press officer Mike Haines. "The real strength came from the emerging markets of Latin America and Asia Pacific and the strong underlying performance in North America," he said.

The Asia-Pacific region turned in a 20 million stg increase in profits to 108 million in the third quarter, Latin America was up 14 million stg at 79 million, while Africa and the Middle East showed a nine million rise to 56 million stg, reflecting changes made by the group to its Nigerian business.
Pretax profits exceeded the stockmarkets forecast range of 760 to 820 million stg, pushing shares 23p higher to 1296p in London. ($1=.6093 Pound)
